Thought: I need to determine why methyl mercaptan is added to natural gas. Let me think about the properties and uses of methyl mercaptan in relation to natural gas.

Methyl mercaptan (CH₃SH) is a chemical compound with a very strong, unpleasant odor similar to rotten cabbage or eggs. Natural gas itself is odorless, which makes gas leaks difficult to detect without special equipment. This poses a significant safety hazard since natural gas is flammable and can cause explosions if it accumulates.

To address this safety concern, odorants like methyl mercaptan are added to natural gas so that people can easily detect leaks by smell, even at very low concentrations. This is a standard safety practice in the natural gas industry.

Looking at the options:
A. To combust the natural gas - No, methyl mercaptan is not added as a combustion agent
B. To help detect leaks due to its bad odor - Yes, this is the correct answer
C. To initiate polymerization - No, this is not the purpose in natural gas
D. To neutralize any acids present - No, this is not why it's added
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
